name: concentration_risk_hhi
summary: Concentration risk via the Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (HHI).
description:
``HHI = sum(w_i^2)`` on absolute weights normalised to sum to 1. Ranges from
``1/n`` (equal weight) to 1 (single holding). The effective number of
holdings is ``1/HHI``.

name: conditional_drawdown_at_risk
summary: Conditional Drawdown at Risk (CDaR).
description:
The mean of the worst ``(1 - confidence_level)`` fraction of drawdowns —
the drawdown analogue of Expected Shortfall (Chekhlov, Uryasev, Zabarankin).

formula.formula_latex: DaR_\alpha = \text{Quantile}_\alpha(DD) \\ CDaR_\alpha = \frac{1}{\left|\{t : DD_t \ge DaR_\alpha\}\right|}\sum_{t:\,DD_t \ge DaR_\alpha} DD_t

name: correlation_clustering
summary: Correlation-based clustering of assets.
description:
Builds the correlation distance ``sqrt(2(1 - rho))`` and performs simple
single-linkage agglomerative clustering down to ``n_clusters`` groups —
grouping assets that co-move.

The merge loop is hand-rolled here rather than calling scikit-learn's
``AgglomerativeClustering`` or SciPy's ``linkage``, though it implements
the same single-linkage algorithm.

formula.caveat: Hand-rolled single-linkage agglomerative clustering (not scikit-learn): repeatedly merges the two clusters with the smallest minimum pairwise correlation-distance until n_clusters groups remain.
formula.formula_latex: d_{ij} = \sqrt{2(1 - \rho_{ij})} \\ D(A,B) = \min_{i \in A,\, j \in B} d_{ij} \;\; \text{(single-linkage merge criterion)}

name: correlation_matrix_portfolio
summary: Correlation matrix and average pairwise correlation of asset returns.

name: currency_attribution
summary: Currency attribution -- naive geometric local/FX decomposition.
description:
Splits the base-currency return into a local-market component and a currency
(FX) component per holding, weighted by exposure, via the geometric
identity ``base = (1+local)(1+fx)-1`` with currency as the residual. The
total reconciles to the weighted base-currency return.

This is NOT Karnosky-Singer (Karnosky, D. & Singer, B. (1994), "The
Currency Dimension of Global Asset Management and Performance
Attribution", CFA Institute Research Foundation) -- that method requires
local-currency return PREMIUMS (local return minus the local risk-free
rate) and moves the interest-rate differential onto the currency side via
covered interest parity; this function takes no interest rates at all. A
prior version of this docstring claimed "Karnosky-Singer style", which is
the same failure mode as this codebase's earlier false QuantLib
cross-validation claim (correct arithmetic, fabricated provenance) --
found during the Tier 3 #2 audit. See Bacon, C. (2008), "Practical
Portfolio Performance Measurement and Attribution", 2nd ed., Ch. 6, which
presents this naive geometric split as the baseline before introducing
Ankrim-Hensel and Karnosky-Singer.

formula.caveat: Naive geometric local/FX split (base=(1+local)(1+fx)-1, currency as residual) -- NOT Karnosky-Singer, which nets local returns against the local risk-free rate; this function takes no interest rates at all.
formula.citation: Bacon, C. (2008), "Practical Portfolio Performance Measurement and Attribution", 2nd ed., Ch. 6
formula.formula_latex: R^{local}_i = w_i r^{L}_i \\ R^{fx}_i = w_i\left[(1+r^{L}_i)(1+r^{FX}_i) - 1 - r^{L}_i\right] \\ R_{total} = \sum_i \left(R^{local}_i + R^{fx}_i\right)

name: cvar_constrained_optimisation
summary: CVaR-constrained portfolio optimisation (Rockafellar-Uryasev).
description:
Maximises expected return subject to the portfolio CVaR (at
``confidence_level``) not exceeding ``cvar_limit``, long-only and fully
invested. CVaR is computed empirically over the supplied scenarios.

CVaR is enforced as a direct nonlinear inequality constraint (the
empirical mean of tail losses) solved by SLSQP, not via Rockafellar and
Uryasev's original auxiliary-variable linear-programming reformulation.

formula.caveat: CVaR is enforced as a nonlinear inequality constraint solved directly by SLSQP (empirical mean of tail losses), not via Rockafellar-Uryasev's original auxiliary-variable linear-programming reformulation.
formula.formula_latex: \max_w\; w^\top \mu \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; 0 \le w_i \le 1,\; CVaR_\alpha(w) \le c \\ L(w) = -R w, \quad VaR_\alpha(w) = \text{Quantile}_\alpha\big(L(w)\big) \\ CVaR_\alpha(w) = \mathbb{E}\big[L(w) \mid L(w) \ge VaR_\alpha(w)\big]

name: diversification_ratio
summary: Diversification ratio — weighted average vol over portfolio vol.
description:
``(w' σ) / sqrt(w' Σ w)`` where ``σ`` is the vector of asset volatilities.
Always >= 1; higher means more diversification benefit (Choueifaty).

name: drawdown_duration
summary: Drawdown duration — longest and current underwater run lengths.
description: Counts consecutive periods spent below the prior peak.

formula.formula_latex: d_t = \begin{cases} 0 & V_t \ge P_t \\ d_{t-1} + 1 & V_t < P_t \end{cases} \\ D_{max} = \max_t d_t

name: equal_weight_portfolio
summary: Equal-weight (1/N) portfolio.

name: esg_score_integration
summary: ESG score integration — weighted score and optional ESG-constrained tilt.
description:
Computes the weighted-average portfolio ESG score. If ``min_esg_score`` and
a covariance matrix are supplied, solves a minimum-variance long-only
portfolio subject to the weighted ESG score meeting the floor.

formula.formula_latex: S_{ESG} = \frac{\sum_i w_i \cdot ESG_i}{\sum_i w_i} \\ \min_w\; w^\top \Sigma w \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; w^\top ESG \ge S_{min},\; 0 \le w_i \le 1

name: factor_based_optimisation
summary: Factor-based minimum-risk optimisation.
description:
Builds the asset covariance from a factor model
``Σ = B F Bᵀ + diag(specific_var)`` and finds the long-only fully-invested
minimum-variance portfolio, optionally matching ``target_exposures`` to the
factors via an equality constraint.

formula.formula_latex: \Sigma = B F B^\top + \text{diag}(\sigma^2_{spec}) \\ \min_w\; w^\top \Sigma w \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; 0 \le w_i \le 1 \;\; \big(\text{optionally } B^\top w = e_{tgt}\big)

name: factor_exposure_analysis_barra
summary: Barra-style portfolio factor exposure.
description:
Aggregates per-asset factor loadings into portfolio-level exposures
``Bᵀ w`` — the active/absolute factor tilts of the portfolio.

formula.formula_latex: E = B^\top w, \quad E_k = \sum_i B_{ik}\, w_i

name: factor_return_attribution
summary: Factor return attribution.
description:
Decomposes the realised portfolio return into per-factor contributions
``exposure_i * factor_return_i`` plus a specific (idiosyncratic) component.

formula.formula_latex: C_i = b_i f_i \\ R_{factor} = \sum_i C_i \\ R_{total} = R_{factor} + \epsilon

name: fama_french_3_factor_model
summary: Fama-French 3-factor regression (MKT, SMB, HML).
description:
Regresses portfolio excess returns on the market, size (SMB) and value
(HML) factors. The intercept is the factor alpha.

name: fama_french_5_factor_model
summary: Fama-French 5-factor regression (MKT, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA).
description: Adds profitability (RMW) and investment (CMA) factors to the 3-factor model.

name: gics_sector_exposure
summary: GICS sector exposure aggregation.
description:
Aggregates position weights into GICS sector buckets and reports each
sector's share of the portfolio. Shares sum to the total invested weight.

name: information_ratio
summary: Information ratio — active return over tracking error.

name: jensens_alpha
summary: Jensen's alpha from the CAPM single-factor regression.
description:
``alpha = mean(r - rf) - beta * mean(b - rf)`` per period; annualised by
multiplication by ``periods_per_year``.

name: liquidity_adjusted_portfolio_var
summary: Liquidity-adjusted parametric VaR (LVaR).
description:
Adds a liquidity cost term equal to half the weighted bid-ask spread to the
parametric delta-normal VaR (Bangia-Diebold-Schuermann simplified add-on),
capturing the cost of unwinding positions.

name: marginal_contribution_to_risk
summary: Marginal and component contribution to portfolio volatility risk.
description:
Marginal contribution ``(Σw)_i / sigma_p``; component ``w_i * marginal_i``.
Component contributions sum exactly to the portfolio volatility (Euler).

formula.formula_latex: \sigma_p = \sqrt{w^\top \Sigma w} \\ MCR_i = \frac{(\Sigma w)_i}{\sigma_p}, \quad CCR_i = w_i \cdot MCR_i, \quad \sum_i CCR_i = \sigma_p

summary: Maximum drawdown — largest peak-to-trough decline.

name: maximum_sharpe_ratio_portfolio
summary: Maximum Sharpe ratio (tangency) portfolio.
description: Maximises the annualised Sharpe ratio subject to weights summing to 1.

name: mean_variance_optimisation
summary: Mean-variance (Markowitz) optimisation.
description:
Maximises ``w'μ - 0.5 * λ * w'Σw`` subject to weights summing to 1, with an
optional long-only constraint.

name: minimum_variance_portfolio
summary: Global minimum-variance portfolio.
description:
Minimises ``w'Σw`` subject to weights summing to 1. With shorting allowed
the closed-form solution ``Σ⁻¹1 / (1'Σ⁻¹1)`` is used; long-only uses SLSQP.

formula.formula_latex: \min_w\; w^\top \Sigma w \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1 \\ w^{*} = \frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}}{\mathbf{1}^\top \Sigma^{-1}\mathbf{1}} \;\; \text{(closed form when shorting allowed)}

name: monte_carlo_portfolio_simulation
summary: Monte Carlo portfolio simulation of terminal P&L.
description:
Draws correlated multivariate-normal asset returns (RULE 3: pre-drawn in
pure Python via Cholesky), compounds them over the horizon in a JIT kernel,
and reports the simulated VaR / ES of terminal P&L.

name: omega_ratio

name: portfolio_turnover

description: ``0.5 * sum(|w_after - w_before|)`` (one-way convention).

name: principal_component_analysis
summary: Principal Component Analysis of an asset return matrix.
description:
Eigendecomposes the covariance matrix to extract orthogonal principal
components ordered by explained variance.

name: rebalancing_optimiser
summary: Rebalancing optimiser with a no-trade band.
description:
Computes the trades to move from current to target weights, suppressing
trades within ``no_trade_band`` to avoid churn, and reports turnover and
total transaction cost.

``no_trade_band`` is a user-supplied absolute weight threshold, not one
derived from cost/volatility parameters the way Leland (1999) or Donohue
& Yip (2003) construct an optimal no-trade region.

formula.formula_latex: \Delta_i = w_i^{tgt} - w_i^{cur} \;\; (\text{set } 0 \text{ if } |\Delta_i| < b) \\ Cost = \sum_i |\Delta_i| \cdot \frac{c_i}{10^4} \\ Turnover = \frac{1}{2}\sum_i |\Delta_i|

name: regime_detection_hmm
summary: Two-state Gaussian regime detection via EM.
description:
Note: despite the name, this fits a stationary 2-component Gaussian
mixture (EM, i.i.d. weights) — there is no transition matrix, so it does
not model true HMM regime persistence/switching dynamics.

Fits a two-component Gaussian mixture by EM and labels each observation by
its most likely regime. The higher-variance component is reported as the
"stress" regime — the standard calm/turbulent market characterisation.

formula.caveat: Despite the _hmm name, this is a STATIONARY 2-component Gaussian mixture fit by EM (i.i.d. weights pi) -- there is no transition matrix, so regime persistence/switching probability is not modelled, only the marginal mixture; it is not a hidden Markov model.
formula.formula_latex: p(x_i) = \pi_0 \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_0,\sigma_0^2) + \pi_1 \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_1,\sigma_1^2) \\ r_{i,k} = \frac{\pi_k \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_k,\sigma_k^2)}{\sum_j \pi_j \mathcal{N}(x_i;\mu_j,\sigma_j^2)} \\ \mu_k = \frac{\sum_i r_{i,k}x_i}{\sum_i r_{i,k}}, \;\; \sigma_k^2 = \frac{\sum_i r_{i,k}(x_i-\mu_k)^2}{\sum_i r_{i,k}}, \;\; \pi_k = \frac{\sum_i r_{i,k}}{n}

name: resampled_efficient_frontier
summary: Resampled efficient frontier (Michaud) minimum-variance point.
description:
Bootstraps return samples from the estimated multivariate-normal, solves the
minimum-variance long-only portfolio on each resample, and averages the
weights — reducing estimation-error sensitivity. All randomness is pre-drawn
in pure Python (RULE 3).

formula.formula_latex: \hat\Sigma^{(k)} = \text{Cov}\big(\text{sample}^{(k)}\big), \;\; \text{sample}^{(k)} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \Sigma, n_{obs}) \\ w^{(k)*} = \arg\min_w\; w^\top \hat\Sigma^{(k)} w \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; 0 \le w_i \le 1 \\ \bar w = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} w^{(k)*}

name: residual_risk
summary: Residual (idiosyncratic) risk — volatility of single-factor regression residuals.
description:
Regresses portfolio returns on the benchmark (CAPM) and reports the
standard deviation of the residuals — the risk not explained by beta.

name: return_attribution_brinson
summary: Brinson-Hood-Beebower return attribution.
description:
Decomposes the active return into allocation, selection and interaction
effects per segment. The three effects sum exactly to the total active
return — the reconciliation property required for performance reporting.

formula.formula_latex: A_i = (w^p_i - w^b_i)(r^b_i - R^b) \\ S_i = w^b_i(r^p_i - r^b_i) \\ I_i = (w^p_i - w^b_i)(r^p_i - r^b_i) \\ R^{active} = \sum_i (A_i + S_i + I_i) = R^p - R^b

name: risk_parity_portfolio
summary: Equal risk contribution (risk parity) portfolio.
description:
Finds long-only weights so each asset contributes equally to portfolio
variance, by minimising the dispersion of risk contributions.

Dispersion is measured as the sum of squared pairwise differences
between all assets' risk contributions rather than each asset's
deviation from the mean contribution -- a stronger gradient signal for
SLSQP that converges to the same equal-risk-contribution solution.

formula.caveat: Equalises risk contributions via an all-pairs sum-of-squared-differences objective (a stronger SLSQP gradient signal than comparing each RC_i to the mean); both formulations converge to the same equal-risk-contribution solution.
formula.formula_latex: RC_i = w_i (\Sigma w)_i \\ \min_w\; \sum_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n} (RC_i - RC_j)^2 \quad \text{s.t. } \sum_i w_i = 1,\; w_i \ge 10^{-6}

name: robust_portfolio_optimisation
summary: Robust mean-variance optimisation with a box uncertainty set on means.

Uses the worst-case expected return ``μ - κ·diag(Σ)^{1/2}`` within an

formula.formula_latex: A_i = (w^p_i - w^b_i)(r^b_i - R^b) \\ S_i = w^b_i(r^p_i - r^b_i) \\ I_i = (w^p_i - w^b_i)(r^p_i - r^b_i) \\ \text{Total}_i = A_i + S_i + I_i

description:
Mean excess return divided by return volatility, annualised by

Volatility is the population standard deviation (divide by n) of
per-period excess returns, not the n-1 sample standard deviation.

name: sortino_ratio
summary: Annualised Sortino ratio.
description:
Like Sharpe but penalises only downside deviation below ``target``, so
upside volatility is not treated as risk.

The numerator's excess return is measured against ``risk_free`` while
the downside-deviation denominator measures shortfalls of the raw (not
risk-free-adjusted) returns below the separate ``target``, so when
``target != risk_free`` the two are distinct reference rates by
construction.

formula.caveat: The numerator's excess return is measured against risk_free while the downside-deviation denominator's threshold is the separate target (MAR) applied to raw (not risk-free-adjusted) returns; when target != risk_free these are two distinct reference rates by construction of this implementation.
formula.formula_latex: Sortino = \sqrt{T} \cdot \frac{\overline{r - r_f}}{DD(MAR)} \\ DD(MAR) = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{t:\, r_t < MAR} (r_t - MAR)^2}

name: transaction_cost_analysis
summary: Transaction Cost Analysis (TCA) — implementation shortfall vs benchmark.
description:
Computes per-trade slippage against an arrival/VWAP benchmark and the
quantity-weighted average slippage in basis points. ``side`` is +1 for
buys (paying above benchmark is a cost) and -1 for sells.

This is narrower than Perold's full implementation-shortfall
decomposition -- there is no delay-cost or unexecuted-share
opportunity-cost leg, so the result is an execution-slippage metric, not
a complete IS attribution.

formula.caveat: Narrower than Perold's full implementation-shortfall decomposition -- no delay cost or unexecuted-share opportunity-cost leg; no published source reproduces this exact quantity.

name: emir_clearing_obligation_check
summary: EMIR clearing obligation check (Art. 4 / Art. 4a / Art. 10 / clearing thresholds).
description:
[REGULATORY] EMIR REFIT (Regulation (EU) 2019/834) Art. 4a(1): a Financial
Counterparty (FC) that breaches its clearing threshold in ANY ONE OTC
derivative asset class becomes subject to the clearing obligation for ALL
asset classes it has positions in, not just the one that breached. Art.
10(1) evaluates a Non-Financial Counterparty above threshold (NFC+)
per-asset-class instead -- only the classes where ITS OWN threshold is
breached become subject to clearing.

A prior version of this function applied FC's per-class-only logic to
BOTH categories (took a single ``asset_class``/``notional`` pair,
identical branching for FC and NFC+ beyond the NFC- exemption). It
understated an FC's clearing scope whenever the breaching class differed
from the queried class -- masked in the original test, which happened to
query the same class that breached. Found during the Tier 3 #2 audit.

formula.formula_latex: any\_breached = \bigvee_{ac} \big(notional_{ac} > threshold_{ac}\big) \\ FC:\ clearing_{ac} = any\_breached\ \ \forall ac \qquad NFC{+}:\ clearing_{ac} = notional_{ac} > threshold_{ac}

description:

correlation and ratio values below, not a single closed-form equation.

amber ``|corr|>=0.70 AND 0.6<=ratio<=1.5``; otherwise red (IMA loss).

name: solvency_ii_scr_credit_risk
summary: Solvency II SCR counterparty default (credit) risk — Type 1 exposures.
description:
The sigma used here is the intra-counterparty (independent-Bernoulli)
variance term only; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 201's
inter-counterparty correlation term is not implemented, so the true
Art. 201 variance (and SCR) is at least as large as what this function
returns.

[REGULATORY] Delegated Regulation (EU) 2015/35 Art. 200(1)-(3) fixes the
capital charge as a TIERED multiplier on the standard deviation (sigma) of
the loss distribution, not a flat 3x: SCR = 3*sigma while
sigma <= 7% of total LGD; SCR = 5*sigma while 7% < sigma/TLGD <= 20%; SCR =
total LGD (fully capped) once sigma/TLGD exceeds 20%. An earlier version of
this function exposed a caller-configurable ``risk_factor`` defaulting to a
flat 3.0 — that understated capital by ~79% on a representative 2-exposure
case (807 vs. the correct ~1449, entirely from missing the 5x/TLGD tiers).
The multiplier is fixed by the Delegated Regulation, so it is intentionally
not a parameter here (same reasoning as CLAUDE.md §4.3/§4.4's Basel
thresholds: never parameterise regulator-set constants).

[LIMITATION] The variance (sigma^2) computed here is the intra-counterparty
term only — an independent-Bernoulli approximation summing each
counterparty's own default-loss variance. Art. 201's full formula also adds
an inter-counterparty correlation term (V_inter) between exposures carrying
different default probabilities, which this implementation does NOT
compute — that term is generally positive, so the true Art. 201 variance
(and therefore the true SCR) is at least as large as what this function
returns. Do not rely on this for statutory Solvency II reporting without an
actuarial review of that gap.

formula.caveat: Per the function's own [LIMITATION] docstring, sigma is the intra-counterparty (independent-Bernoulli) variance term only; Art. 201's inter-counterparty correlation term (V_inter) is not computed, so the true Art. 201 SCR is at least as large as this result.
formula.formula_latex: LGD_i = EAD_i \times LGD^{rate}_i \\ TLGD = \sum_i LGD_i \\ \sigma = \sqrt{\sum_i LGD_i^2\, PD_i (1 - PD_i)} \\ SCR = \begin{cases} 3\sigma & \sigma / TLGD \le 0.07 \\ 5\sigma & 0.07 < \sigma / TLGD \le 0.20 \\ TLGD & \sigma / TLGD > 0.20 \end{cases}

description:
The SRRI class itself is a bucket lookup of the annualised volatility
against fixed CESR volatility bands, not a closed-form equation.

Maps the annualised volatility of (weekly by default) returns to the SRRI
bucket per CESR 10-673: class 1 (< 0.5%) up to class 7 (>= 25%).

formula.caveat: The SRRI class (1-7) is a bucket lookup of \sigma_{ann} against fixed CESR volatility bands, not itself a closed-form equation -- shown above is the annualised volatility that feeds the lookup.
